system_description.narrative_title: U.S.–Iran escalation spreads to Red Sea, oil and regional theatres
system_description.narrative_summary: News in this window is dominated by an escalating U.S.–Iran confrontation that is spreading across the Middle East — notably into the Red Sea, the Strait of Hormuz and allied Gulf states — producing military strikes, proxy attacks and synchronized market shocks. Treated as an open system, the story comprises interacting actors (U.S., Iran, Houthis, Saudi/Gulf militaries, Israel, regional partners), flows (forces, weapons, information, oil shipments and insurance), and reinforcing feedbacks (retaliation cycles, market volatility driving strategic choices, alliance signalling). Porous boundaries allow external actors and economic shocks (global oil demand, insurers, shipping rerouting, diplomatic initiatives) to enter or dampen the escalation, producing nonlinear risk of broader war and supply disruption.
system_description.scope: Military-diplomatic-economic interactions among the U.S., Iran, Iran-aligned proxies (notably Houthis), Gulf states and maritime commerce in the Middle East (Red Sea, Strait of Hormuz, adjacent seas), including energy markets, insurance and shipping routes.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-security and energy system (international order, global oil markets, and maritime commerce).
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil markets and maritime logistics (tankers, Suez route, insurance)
Regional proxy and militia networks (Iran-Houthi axis, Gulf coalitions)
U.S. domestic politics and military logistics (force posture, munitions stocks, presidential decision-making)
International diplomacy and mediation channels (Oman, Pakistan, China, UN, bilateral talks)

variables.name: Escalation intensity
variables.description: Measures the overall rate and severity of reciprocal military and proxy actions and kinetic incidents across the region.

variables.name: Proxy attack rate
variables.description: Measures the frequency of armed strikes and incursions carried out by aligned non-state or proxy forces per unit time.

variables.name: Conventional force levels
variables.description: Measures the aggregate deployed strength and concentration of conventional military assets in regional theaters.

variables.name: Maritime transit volume
variables.description: Measures the number and gross tonnage of commercial vessel transits through strategic sea routes per unit time.

variables.name: Oil supply flow
variables.description: Measures the volume of crude oil and refined product shipments originating from or transiting the regional export corridors per unit time.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: Measures prevailing market prices for benchmark crude reflecting perceived and actual supply-demand imbalances.

variables.name: Insurance coverage availability
variables.description: Measures the extent and willingness of commercial insurers to offer war-risk and hull coverage for shipping in the affected waters.

variables.name: Shipping rerouting cost
variables.description: Measures additional monetary and time costs incurred when commercial shipping avoids high-risk routes and uses longer alternatives.

variables.name: Alliance cohesion
variables.description: Measures the degree of coordination, policy alignment, and joint operational intent among cooperating security partners.

variables.name: Deterrence perception
variables.description: Measures actors' perceived credibility and effectiveness of retaliatory capabilities held by adversaries and partners.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement rate
variables.description: Measures the intensity and frequency of formal and informal diplomatic contacts, negotiations and mediation efforts.

variables.name: Market volatility level
variables.description: Measures short-term fluctuation amplitude in financial and commodity markets tied to regional risk perceptions and shocks.

variables.name: Command-and-control resilience
variables.description: Measures the robustness and redundancy of military command, control, communications, and decision-making under stress or attack.

variables.name: Weapons arsenal capacity
variables.description: Measures the available inventory and ready-to-use stock of strike weapons (missiles, munitions, naval/air ordnance) in the theater.

variables.name: Information flow rate
variables.description: Measures the tempo and volume of intelligence, public messaging, media reports, and signaling exchanged among actors and publics.

variables.name: Escalation aversion
variables.description: Measures political and military appetite among leaders and publics for accepting further escalation versus seeking restraint.

catalysts.title: U.S.–Iran talks and bombing pause
catalysts.description: Ongoing diplomatic talks and an announced U.S. pause in strikes create a window for negotiations that could lower kinetic exchanges.
catalysts.rationale: "U.S. pauses Iran strikes"; "US pauses Iran strikes as Oman pursues Hormuz transit deal"; "Trump says US is talking with Iran"

catalysts.title: Resumption of U.S. kinetic strikes
catalysts.description: Renewed U.S. strikes or a large punitive strike campaign against Iran or proxies, driven by political decisions or new incidents.
catalysts.rationale: "Trump considers ‘massive attack’ on Iran"; "Trump says he is ready for military action if Iran talks fail"; "US strikes Iran after American troops killed"

catalysts.title: Houthis expand Red Sea attacks
catalysts.description: Continued and widening Houthi strikes against shipping and energy infrastructure in the Red Sea and related corridors.
catalysts.rationale: "Houthis fire on Saudi Red Sea oil sites"; "Houthis say they targeted Saudi east-west oil transport"; "Red Sea shipping slows"

catalysts.title: Saudi and Gulf strikes on Houthi targets
catalysts.description: Continued Saudi-led kinetic strikes against Houthi positions in Yemen in retaliation for attacks on shipping and energy sites.
catalysts.rationale: "Saudi military strikes Houthi targets in Yemen"; "Saudi strikes Houthis after militia attacked Red Sea shipping"

catalysts.title: U.S. surge of forces toward Middle East
catalysts.description: Ongoing deployments and reinforcement of U.S. conventional forces into regional theaters, expanding operational options and signaling.
catalysts.rationale: "U.S. Surges Forces Toward Middle East, Giving Trump Options to Expand Iran War"; "U.S. Surges Forces Toward Middle East"

catalysts.title: Increased rerouting via Suez and longer voyages
catalysts.description: Commercial shipping shifts away from high-risk Gulf and Red Sea routes toward Suez and longer voyages, raising costs and transit times.
catalysts.rationale: "Tanker switches Asia voyage via Suez"; "Add a month at sea and $2.5 million"; "Saudi oil exports increasingly depend on Suez"

catalysts.title: Netanyahu meeting with Trump on Iran
catalysts.description: High-level U.S.–Israel talks where Iran policy is front-and-center, likely to shape allied posture and signaling toward Tehran.
catalysts.rationale: "Netanyahu says Iran is top agenda in meeting with Trump"; earlier 'Netanyahu will visit US next week'

catalysts.title: Washington–London meeting to resolve Hormuz crisis
catalysts.description: Planned talks between US and UK (and possibly partners) to arrange protections or transit mechanisms for the Strait of Hormuz.
catalysts.rationale: "Washington and London discuss plan for meeting to resolve Hormuz crisis"; 'Oman pursues Hormuz transit deal'

catalysts.title: Insurance restrictions on Red Sea cargoes
catalysts.description: Commercial insurers restrict war-risk/hull coverage for Red Sea and Saudi-related cargoes, altering risk calculus for shippers.
catalysts.rationale: "Ship insurers restrict war coverage for Saudi Arabian cargoes in Red Sea"; "Tanker switches Asia voyage via Suez"

catalysts.title: U.S. munitions and air-defense stock constraints
catalysts.description: Reported depletion concerns over missiles and air-defense stocks that constrain operational tempo and political willingness for strikes.
catalysts.rationale: "How Many U.S. Missiles Are Left?"; "Trump Pauses Iran Strikes as Officials Weigh Dwindling Air Defense Stocks"
